The lighthouse was built in 1854 on a granite outcrop at the mouth of the harbor, replacing an earlier wooden tower destroyed by a winter storm. Its lamp, originally fueled by whale oil, was converted to electricity in 1923 and automated in 1968, ending more than a century of resident keepers. Today the structure is maintained by a local preservation society and remains an active aid to navigation, its white flash visible up to eighteen nautical miles out to sea.
